title: Working with LLM APIs (Orchestration)
summary: Turn single LLM API calls into reliable software: messages, streaming, structured outputs, tools, orchestration, concurrency, failure handling and observability.
outcome: Build applications that combine LLM calls, software logic, external tools and reliability controls, without RAG or autonomous agents.

project.title: Streaming Tool-Using Assistant
deliverables: Conversational assistant with history, system instructions and streamed responses
Integrate at least 2-3 real tools or APIs
Sequential or parallel tool use, validating every model-generated argument
Structured outputs where useful, retries for transient failures and enforced timeouts
Graceful handling of tool and API errors
Record token usage, latency, retries, tool calls and estimated cost
Build the main implementation with LangChain and explain the raw API and tool-call mechanics underneath

modules.title: First API calls & conversation state

topics.d: Calling OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs: roles, system instructions, stop reasons and usage.
History must be resent explicitly because the API keeps no state.
What the app stores versus what is in the current window.
Env vars, .env files or secret managers, never in frontend code.
Read token counts and metadata instead of treating the API as prompt-to-string.

modules.outcome: Make multi-turn API calls to two providers, managing history, keys and usage data yourself.

modules.title: Streaming

topics.d: Display partial output in a terminal or UI as it arrives.
Time to first token, generation speed, perceived and total latency.
Assemble events into a full response; handle cancellation and broken streams.

modules.outcome: Stream responses to a user and handle cancelled or incomplete streams.

modules.title: LangChain fundamentals

topics.d: What LangChain abstracts over raw SDKs.
Chat models, prompt templates, parsers, streaming and configuration.
Swapping providers while knowing the underlying calls.
Chaining prompts, models and parsers with runnables.
Comparing equivalent implementations for convenience vs overhead.

topics.t: LangChain is a layer, not the model
topics.d: It orchestrates calls; it is not the LLM.

modules.outcome: Build the same small pipeline with a raw SDK and with LangChain and explain the trade-offs.

modules.title: Structured outputs

topics.d: Constrain output with a schema rather than asking nicely for JSON.
JSON Schema or Pydantic with required/optional fields, enums, lists and nesting.
Native structured-output features vs LangChain abstractions.
Check outputs before they reach application logic.
Well-formed output can still be wrong.
Accept, retry, repair or reject invalid outputs.

modules.outcome: Get reliably typed, validated data out of a model and handle invalid outputs.

modules.title: Function / tool calling

topics.d: The model picks a tool and arguments; your code runs it.
Names, descriptions, parameter schemas and required arguments.
User input, model request, execution, result back, final answer.
Matching IDs and inserting results correctly into the conversation.
Direct tool calling and how LangChain wraps it.
Dependent, repeated and parallel calls in one turn.
Handling failing tools and bad arguments.

modules.outcome: Implement the complete tool-calling loop by hand, including parallel calls and failures.

modules.title: Designing good tools

topics.d: Precise names, clear descriptions, minimal params, strong types and useful errors.
Overlap leads the model to pick the wrong tool.
Avoid large sets of similar tools and needless arguments.
Validate types, values, permissions and destructive operations.
Descriptions shape the model's decisions.

modules.outcome: Design a tool set the model selects correctly and that is safe to execute.

modules.title: Multi-step LLM workflows

topics.d: Combining multiple calls, tools, transformations and code.
Pipelines, routing, conditional branches and fan-out/fan-in.
Specialized calls vs one big prompt.
Hand-built control flow first, then LangChain primitives.
Application-controlled flows vs model-controlled agents.

modules.outcome: Build a multi-step workflow whose control flow lives in your code.

modules.title: Async, concurrency & batching

topics.d: Sync vs async calls and when concurrency raises throughput.
Process independent requests in parallel.
Cap concurrency to avoid rate-limit failures.
Async and batch APIs in SDKs and orchestration tools.
Throughput vs latency, limits, resources and cost.

modules.outcome: Process many LLM requests quickly without tripping rate limits.

modules.title: Robustness: retries, timeouts & fallbacks

topics.d: Auth errors, bad requests, rate limits, 5xx, timeouts, context limits and malformed output.

topics.t: What to retry and what to fail fast
topics.d: Retry transient errors; fail fast on auth and invalid requests.
Exponential backoff with jitter, retry caps, timeouts and graceful degradation.
Falling back to other models or providers, minding behavior differences.

topics.t: Failures at the LLM and tool levels
topics.d: Handling both model API and tool API failures.
SDK, orchestration layer or application code.

modules.outcome: Make an LLM app survive rate limits, outages and timeouts gracefully.

modules.title: Cost, usage & observability

topics.d: Model, tokens, latency, retries, errors, tool calls and estimated cost.
One multi-step interaction is one trace.
Which step failed, used most tokens or added latency.
LangChain callbacks and tracing to link model and tool calls.

topics.t: Logging you can actually debug with
topics.d: Structured logs and traces instead of scattered prints.

modules.outcome: Trace a workflow end to end and explain where its time and money went.

modules.title: Other orchestration frameworks

topics.t: LangChain is one approach among many
topics.d: Not a universal standard.
How LlamaIndex's abstractions and focus differ.
Branches, loops, persistent state and complex control flow.
A graph-based approach for stateful LLM workflows.
Declaring input/output behavior instead of hand-writing prompts.
Speed, overhead, debugging, portability, state and control.
Raw SDK, LangChain, graph frameworks, LlamaIndex, DSPy or custom.

modules.outcome: Choose an orchestration approach based on the application, not habit.

modules.title: Capstone: Streaming Tool-Using Assistant

topics.t: A streaming assistant with real tools
topics.d: History, system instructions, streaming and 2-3 real tools.
Validated arguments for every generated call.
Structured outputs, transient retries, timeouts and graceful tool errors.
Tokens, latency, retries, tool calls and cost per request.

topics.t: Building on LangChain, explaining the raw calls
topics.d: LangChain implementation with raw mechanics explained.
All combined without RAG or autonomous agents.

modules.outcome: A reliable, observable streaming assistant that uses real tools.
